title: Ahom kingdom
sub: From Assampedia, the free Assam encyclopedia
body:
The Ahom kingdom ruled much of the Brahmaputra Valley for about 600 years, from 1228 to 1826. It was founded by Sukaphaa, a Tai prince who came from present-day Myanmar and settled first at Charaideo.

The Ahoms are remembered for holding off Mughal invasions — most famously at the Battle of Saraighat in 1671, led by the general Lachit Borphukan — and for their system of administration, land records and chronicles known as buranjis.
extra:
Administration

The Ahoms divided the kingdom into khels and used the paik system, in which adult males served the state in rotation. Their court kept buranjis — detailed chronicles — which are a major source for Assam's history.

Monuments

Ahom monuments survive around Sivasagar: Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar, the Sivasagar tank, Joysagar tank and the Charaideo maidams (burial mounds), now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
